# Text

Body text in the theme's type scale and colors. Renders a `<p>` by default.

```tsx
import { Text } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/text/text";
```

## Example

```tsx
<Text>Braise for three hours.</Text>
<Text size="sm" tone="muted">Updated 2 days ago</Text>
<Text tone="destructive">Could not save the recipe.</Text>
<Text lines={2}>{recipe.description}</Text>
```

## Usage

Inside a `Button`, pass plain text as children; the button styles it.

## Use instead when

- Use `Heading` instead for titles (it renders `<h1>`–`<h6>`).

## Props

Props every mode takes. Type: `TextProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | inherited | Alignment in writing direction. |
| `as` | `"p" \| "span" \| "div"` | `"p"` | The element to render. Use `span` inside other text, `div` around block content. |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The text. Inline elements such as `<strong>` and `<a>` are fine inside. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, width, grid placement (`mt-2`, `max-w-prose`). Appearance classes warn in development; use `size`, `tone` and `align`. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  | Reaches the rendered element. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Type size from the theme. |
| `tone` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "destructive" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "default" \| "muted"` | `"default"` | Text color: `default` foreground, `muted` for secondary text, or a tone for status text (`destructive` for an error). `secondary` is the same as `muted`, because shadcn's `--secondary` is a surface color, not a text color. |

## Modes

`TextProps` is a union: pass the props of exactly one mode. Mixing them is a type error.

### With `lines`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lines` | `number` |  | Clamps the text to this many lines with an ellipsis. Use `truncate` for one line. |

Not in this mode (typed `never`):

- `truncate`: Not with `lines`. Use `truncate` for one line or `lines` for more, not both.

### With `truncate`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `truncate` | `boolean` |  | Cuts the text to one line with an ellipsis. Use `lines` for more than one line. |

Not in this mode (typed `never`):

- `lines`: Not with `truncate`. Use `truncate` for one line or `lines` for more, not both.

## Native attributes

Also accepts the attributes in React's `HTMLAttributes` (`id`, `aria-*`, event handlers), passed to the rendered element, except those named on this page.

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `color`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `tone`: `<Text tone="muted">`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: each component merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with the component's own replaces it.

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: use the `align` prop.
